The graph above shows the curve $y=k{(\frac{1}{2})}^{x}+c.$ Find the value of $k-c.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote of the curve $y=k{(\frac{1}{2})}^{x}+c$ is $y=c.$ In the graph above, the horizontal asymptote is $y=2.5.$ Hence, $c=2.5.$

We can solve for $k$ by finding a point on the graph and substituting for $x$ and $y.$ The labeled point on the graph is $(0,2.75),$ so we substitute $x=0$ and $y=2.75$ into the function and solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}k{(\frac{1}{2})}^{x}+c & =y \\ k{(\frac{1}{2})}^{x}+2.5 & =y \\ k{(\frac{1}{2})}^{0}+2.5 & =2.75 \\ k+2.5 & =2.75 \\ k & =0.25.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
k-c=0.25-2.5=-2.25.
$$

The equation of the curve is $y=0.25{(\frac{1}{2})}^{x}+2.5.$
